record.name: Compatible weight averaging and regressions
record.role: Check parameter alignment before averaging and evaluate the resulting function.
record.description: Weight averaging combines numbers at matching parameter coordinates. Shape equality is necessary but does not prove semantic alignment: hidden units can be permuted while preserving the original function. Independently trained models can therefore disagree about which coordinate represents which feature. A shared initialization and compatible training recipe make an average more interpretable, but do not guarantee that every task is preserved. An averaged checkpoint also needs an explicit optimizer policy; averaging weights does not establish suitable Adam moments or a resume cursor.
mechanism: Check architecture, tokenizer, parameter order and source checkpoint identities.
Form a declared weighted average only across compatible coordinates.
Evaluate both original checkpoints and the average on identical reserved cases.
Treat averaged weights as a new model identity and explicitly choose fresh or otherwise justified optimizer state.
record.learningObjective: Check parameter alignment before averaging and evaluate the resulting function.
record.engineeringExample: Two equivalent two-unit linear networks represent y=x with incoming vector [1,−1] and outgoing [0.5,−0.5], or with both vectors permuted to [−1,1] and [−0.5,0.5]. Each dot product is 1. Averaging corresponding incoming and outgoing entries gives zeros, so the averaged network produces y=0. By contrast, averaging compatible scalar weights 1 and 3 gives 2; that arithmetic alone still does not predict task quality.
record.evidenceNotes: Mode: worked example. Compatible parameter coordinates and tokenizer required. Permutation counterexample is an exact linear network; no averaging feature is executed by the lifecycle core.
